0.long_answer: The neurosurgical procedure that can result in a complete reversal of Foix–Chavany–Marie syndrome symptoms when such symptoms are caused by epileptic discharges is the resective surgery targeting the insulo‐opercular region. In cases of intractable epilepsy, particularly when the epileptic focus is localized within the insulo‐opercular cortex, removing the epileptogenic tissue can eliminate the abnormal discharges that lead to the syndrome. Several studies and case reports have shown that surgical resection in this region can lead to a complete reversal of the symptoms associated with Foix–Chavany–Marie syndrome, also known as the bilateral opercular syndrome.
0.short_answer: Resective surgery of the insulo-opercular region
